G.A., Satendra Kumar 
 Court No. - 64
 Hon'Ble Samit Gopal, J. 
1.
List revised.

2. Heard Sri Rakesh Chandra Upadhyay, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Satendra Kumar,
learned counsel for the first informant and Sri Ajay Singh, learned AGA-I for the State and perused the material on record.
3.

This bail application under Section 483 of B.N.S.S. has been filed by the applicant Sandeep Kumar Jaiswal @ Prashant, seeking enlargement on bail during trial in connection with Case Crime No. 488 of 2024, under Sections 354-Ka, 354-Kha, 452, 504, 506, 376-AB IPC and Section 5m/6 POCSO Act, registered at Police Station Robertsganj, District Sonbhadra.

4. The FIR of the matter was lodged on 05.07.2024 by Smt. Vibha Jaiswal against the applicant alleging therein that on 08.06.2024 at about 09:00 pm her daughter aged about 12 years was studying in room wherein the applicant reached there and enraged her modesty and had an intention to commit rape upon her wherein she raised a shout and then she came there and saved her.
The applicant then at about 09:30 pm while hurling abuses threatened her for life and ran away.
Report be lodged and action be taken.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case.

It is submitted that the applicant was initially granted bail vide order dated 01.02.2025 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Sonbhadra in third Bail Application No. 144 of 2025 (Sandeep Jaiswal Vs. Government of Uttar Pradesh) in the present case under Sections 354-Ka, 354-Kha, 452, 504, 506 IPC and Section 7/8 POCSO Act, 2012 and at that time charge sheet was submitted which was also observed by the court concerned in para 7 of the said order.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Sonbhadra
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Sandeep Jaiswal Vs. Government of Uttar Pradesh)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that after submission of charge sheet, the first informant made an objection before the Superintendent of Police, Sonbhadra regarding the same and the first charge sheet No. A438 of 2024 dated 19.08.2024 although was submitted in a court but the matter was directed to be further investigated after which Section 7/8 of POCSO Act was deleted and Section 376AB IPC and 5m/6 POCSO Act was added and then charge sheet No. 3 dated 17.04.2025 as a supplementary charge sheet was submitted on which the court concerned took cognizance vide order dated 07.05.2025.

It is submitted that during further investigation no such new material has surfaced in the present matter and although three witnesses namely Jaishree, Smt. Meera Devi and Smt. Raj Kumari were interrogated but no new material has surfaced in their statements.

It is submitted that even the first informant during investigation in her statement recorded under Section 180 BNSS has reiterated the version given by her in the FIR and further states that she was in relationship with the applicant since long and there was some discussion between them for Sandeep Kumar Jaiswal Alias Prashant vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199444165/
2 marriage and the applicant had established physical relationship with her.

sentences.text: It is submitted that the implication of the applicant in the present matter is without credible evidence and even in further investigation no such credible evidence has surfaced in it.
It is submitted while placing supplementary affidavit dated 29.07.2025 that the first informant has been examined as PW-1 before the trial court who has not supported the prosecution case.

It is further submitted that another First Information Report was lodged by the first informant against the applicant as Case Crime No. 42 of 2024, under Sections 376, 506 IPC, P.S. Machi, District Sonbhadra in which he has been granted bail vide order dated 17.12.2024 passed by the Additional District and Sessions Judge (FTC) (CAW), Sonbhadra, copy of the order has been produced before the Court which is annexure S.A.1 to the said supplementary affidavit.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge (FTC) (CAW), Sonbhadra
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the applicant has no other criminal history except two cases which is explained as stated in para 55 of the affidavit and is in jail since 20.05.2025.
6. Learned counsel for the first informant although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the arguments aforesaid.
Learned counsel for the State vehemently opposed the prayer for bail.

7. After having heard learned counsels for the parties and perusing the records, it is evident that the applicant was initially granted bail vide order dated 01.02.2025 passed by the Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Sonbhadra in third Bail Application No. 144 of 2025 (Sandeep Jaiswal Vs. Government of Uttar Pradesh), under Sections 354-Ka, 354-Kha, 452, 504, 506 IPC and Section 7/8 POCSO Act, 2012 and on that time charge sheet has already been submitted in the said sections.

entities.text: Additional Sessions Judge/Special Judge (POCSO Act), Sonbhadra
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: third Bail Application No. 144 of 2025 (Sandeep Jaiswal Vs. Government of Uttar Pradesh)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The first informant made an objection before the Superintendent of Police, Sonbhadra against the said charge sheet on which further investigation was done and then Section 7/8 POCSO Act was deleted and Section 376-AB IPC and 5m/6 POCSO Act was added and then a supplementary charge sheet dated 17.04.2025 was submitted.
The first informant and the applicant were in relationship since long and there was some discussion for marriage between them which could not materialize.

8. Looking to the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence and also the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence, this Court is of the view that the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

9. Let the applicant Sandeep Kumar Jaiswal @ Prashant, be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
i) The applicant will not tamper with prosecution evidence and will not harm or harass the victim/complainant in any manner whatsoever.
ii) The applicant will abide the orders of court, will attend the court on every date and will not delay the disposal of trial in any manner whatsoever.
Sandeep Kumar Jaiswal Alias Prashant vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 8 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/199444165/
3

entities.text: Sandeep Kumar Jaiswal Alias Prashant vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iii) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in court.
In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(iv) The applicant will not misuse the liberty of bail in any manner whatsoever.

In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under section 82 Cr.P.C. may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under section 174-A I.P.C.
(v) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law and the trial court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.
(vi) The trial court may make all possible efforts/endeavour and try to conclude the trial expeditiously after the release of the applicant.

10. The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned and in case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail and send the applicant to prison.
11.
The bail application is allowed.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
